verdicts.reason: The quote only describes the SDC as the executable form of the tables. It is a documentation statement with nothing to verify or exercise in simulation, and the rule adds a 'must' that the quote doesn't contain.

The quote states that every changing output is a flip-flop Q pin with a one-cycle-minus-clk-to-q budget. That is a structural and timing property, so it can't be checked from interface signals each cycle, and check=none is right. The quote's own wording is descriptive, but it is a design constraint on outputs, so the rule is kept as is. The actor is the IP, which drives both the APB4 and TL-UL outputs. The APB4 outputs come from the bridge acting as APB master and the TL-UL outputs from it acting as TL-UL host, so 'master' is acceptable.
The quote says no exceptions are needed, which is a description of the SDC contents. It is not a testable behavioural rule, and nothing in simulation can verify or exercise it.
The quote says there is no requirement. It only offers a placement recommendation for the integrator, which is a physical-design matter with nothing to verify.
This is an optional physical-design note for the integrator about buffering. It has no functional behaviour to verify or exercise.
